To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the path loss exponent for the LOS case at 28 GHz for the omnidirectional model is 1.1 for vertically-polarization, (ii) the mean delay spread at 28 GHz is 18.4ns and the maximum is 193ns, (iii) the path loss for the NLOS case at 28GHz for the omnidirection model is 3.2,
the path loss exponents for the 28 GHz and the 73 GHz channels are significantly lower than the free space path loss exponents and the delay spreads are larger than in the lower microwave bands.
the 28 GHz and the 73 GHz path loss exponents in LOS and NLOS were 1.2 and 3.3 and 2.1 and 3.5, respectively.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the characterization of the radio wave propagation at 28 GHz in a typical indoor environment.
the propagation characteristics of the 28 and 73 GHz bands in indoor environments.
developing millimeter-wave propagation channel models and channel sounders for the design of future 5G wireless networks.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the path loss exponents are lower than those predicted by the 3GPP 36.873 standard, but the delay spread values are similar to those measured at 60 GHz.
the 73 GHz path loss exponent was higher than at 28 GHz, the RMS delay spread was smaller and the maximum path loss was lower at 73 GHz than at 28GHz.
the propagation channel at 28 GHz is similar to that of the 73 GHz channel, but with slightly higher attenuation, slightly higher delay spread, and slightly higher penetration loss.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

28 GHz and higher millimeter-wave frequencies are well suited for indoor applications, with path loss exponents in the range of 1.1-3.2, and that the RMS delay spread values are in the range of a few ns to 100s of ns.
the 73 GHz measurements were more challenging than the 28 GHz measurements due to higher path loss, higher delay spreads and higher antenna gains.
the path loss exponent in a typical office indoor environment is approximately 2 at both 28 GHz and at 73 GHz, but the delay spreads are significantly different.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the millimeter wave propagation channel exhibits a much lower path loss and delay spread at 28 GHz compared to 73 GHz.
the 28 GHz and especially 73 GHz path loss exponents are much lower than the 4.0 exponent predicted by the ITU-R 838-3 model for 10-20 GHz.

the path loss exponent is lower in the 28 GHz and the 73 GHz bands compared to the 5 GHz band and that the RMS delay spread is significantly higher in the 73 GHz band compared to the 28 GHz band, which will require more advanced signal processing techniques to mitigate the effects of multipath fading.
